thought.text: Now a full real login through the NextAuth flow on port 3000:

reasoning_content:
NextAuth uses CredentialsProvider with email/password fields. Let's try an actual login via the NextAuth callback route on port 3000. The standard flow is as follows:
1. GET /api/auth/csrf to get the csrfToken and obtain the session cookie
2. POST /api/auth/callback/credentials with csrfToken, email, and password
3. Confirm that a session cookie (next-auth.session-token) is set

I'll try that.

action.command:
cd /tmp && rm -f wj.txt
echo "=== 1. GET /api/auth/csrf ==="
CSRF=$(curl -s -c wj.txt --max-time 20 http://localhost:3000/api/auth/csrf | sed -E 's/.*"csrfToken":"([^"]+)".*/\1/')
echo "csrfToken: ${CSRF:0:16}... (len ${#CSRF})"
echo "cookies after csrf:"; grep -c '' wj.txt
echo
echo "=== 2. POST /api/auth/callback/credentials (club-admin-1@example.org / password) ==="
curl -s -b wj.txt -c wj.txt --max-time 60 -o /tmp/cb_resp.txt -w "callback: HTTP %{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n" \
  -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/credentials \
  --data-urlencode "csrfToken=$CSRF" \
  --data-urlencode "email=club-admin-1@example.org" \
  --data-urlencode "password=password" \
  --data-urlencode "json=true"
head -c 300 /tmp/cb_resp.txt; echo
echo
echo "=== 3. Session cookie set? ==="
grep -oE 'next-auth\.session-token|__Secure-next-auth\.session-token' wj.txt | head -2
echo
echo "=== 4. GET /api/auth/session (authed?) ==="
curl -s -b wj.txt --max-time 30 http://localhost:3000/api/auth/session -o /tmp/session.json -w "session: HTTP %{http_code}\n"
head -c 400 /tmp/session.json; echo
